title: cli: new @usearazzo/cli package — proposed command surface

raw.title: cli: new @usearazzo/cli package — proposed command surface
raw.body:
## Problem

The root README has carried a `-- Placeholder --` CLI section pointing at `./packages/cli/README.md` since the beginning — but no `packages/cli` exists. Meanwhile the toolkit's programmatic surface is complete enough to wrap: workflow execution (`WorkflowExecutor.execute`), standalone step execution (`StepExecutor.execute`), Arazzo-agnostic operation execution (`OpenAPIOperationExecutor.execute`), validation (`@usearazzo/validator`), and — once #82 and #83 land — workflow enumeration and execution-profile analysis. A CLI is the natural delivery vehicle for all of it, and it is also the designated home for the conveniences we deliberately keep out of the library (environment-variable interpolation, timeouts as a flag, human-readable rendering).

This issue proposes the package and documents the suggested command surface. Interface sketches previously attached to #82 and #83 are consolidated here; this issue is the source of truth for the CLI surface.

## Package

- `packages/cli`, published as `@usearazzo/cli`, bin name **`arazzo`**.
- Node `>= 20.10.0`, ESM; no browser build (the CLI is exactly the environment-coupled layer the library refuses to be).
- Thin wrappers only: every command delegates to an existing programmatic API — the CLI must not grow execution/analysis logic of its own.
- Root README placeholder section replaced with real content linking to the package README.

## Proposed command surface

### Discovery

```
arazzo list-workflows <document-uri> [--json]
```
Enumerates workflows (id, summary) of an Arazzo document. Wraps `ArazzoDocument.listWorkflows()` (#83). Human table by default; `--json` emits `WorkflowDescriptor[]`.

```
arazzo describe-workflow <document-uri> <workflow-id> [--json]
```
Human-readable overview of one workflow: description, inputs (from the `inputs` schema), steps with the operation each resolves to, declared outputs, security requirements and where they apply, server variables. A pure rendering of the execution profile (#82) — no analysis logic in the CLI. `--json` emits the profile itself.

```
arazzo analyze-workflow <document-uri> <workflow-id> [--fill-examples] [--format yaml|json] [-o <file>]
```
Emits the execution profile artifact (#82) with empty value slots, ready to be filled and passed to `execute-workflow --profile`. `--fill-examples` pre-fills `inputs.values` with schema-derived placeholder values. Default format `yaml`, default destination stdout.

### Execution

```
arazzo execute-workflow <document-uri> <workflow-id>
  [--inputs <json|@file>]
  [--profile <file>]
  [--server <url>] [--server-variable <name>=<value>]...
  [--timeout <ms>]
  [--json]
```
Runs a workflow to completion via `WorkflowExecutor.execute`. `--profile` supplies a filled execution profile (#82) pre-configuring inputs, securities, and servers; explicit flags override profile values. `--timeout` maps to `AbortSignal.timeout` (the library's caller-owned time-boxing, surfaced as a flag). Output: human summary of the run (status, per-step results, outputs) by default; `--json` emits the full `WorkflowExecutionResult` trace.

```
arazzo execute-operation <document-uri> (--operation-id <id> | --operation-path <path>)
  [--parameters <json|@file>] [--request-body <json|@file>]
  [--profile <file>] [--server <url>] [--timeout <ms>] [--json]
```
Runs a single OpenAPI operation via `OpenAPIOperationExecutor.execute` — works against a bare OpenAPI document, no Arazzo document required.

### Validation

```
arazzo validate <document-uri> [--json]
```
Wraps `@usearazzo/validator`; human-readable diagnostics by default, structured with `--json`. Exit code reflects validity.

## Conventions (all commands)

- `<document-uri>`: local path or http(s) URL, resolved through the same registry/resolver machinery the runner uses; `-` reads the document from stdin.
- `@file` argument form reads JSON/YAML from a file; a bare value is parsed as inline JSON.
- `--json` everywhere for machine-readable output on stdout; human rendering is the default. Diagnostics and progress go to stderr, never stdout.
- **Environment-variable interpolation** of `${VAR}` references happens in the CLI when loading a `--profile` (and `@file` inputs) — this is the CLI-side counterpart to the library's "no `process.env`" rule (#82), so profiles with secret slots can be committed and hydrated at run time.
- Exit codes: `0` success (workflow `completed`/`ended`, document valid); `1` run failed / document invalid; `2` usage, parse, or resolution error.
- `--version`, `--help` per command; errors surface the library's structured error `reason` codes verbatim.

## Suggested phasing

1. Scaffold + `validate` + `execute-workflow`/`execute-operation` (wrap what exists today).
2. `list-workflows` (needs #83).
3. `analyze-workflow` + `describe-workflow` + `--profile` support on the execute commands (needs #82).

## Out of scope

- Any analysis or execution logic in the CLI itself (lives in the runner/validator).
- OAuth token acquisition (see #82 constraints — profiles carry already-acquired credentials).
- Interactive/TUI modes, watch mode — possible follow-ups, not part of the initial surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/cli` exists, published as `@usearazzo/cli` with bin `arazzo`, wired into the lerna build/test/lint pipeline.
- [ ] Phase-1 commands (`validate`, `execute-workflow`, `execute-operation`) implemented as thin wrappers with the conventions above.
- [ ] `--json` output is stable and documented; humans get stderr diagnostics, machines get clean stdout.
- [ ] `${VAR}` interpolation implemented for `--profile`/`@file` loading, with a test proving the library itself never touches `process.env`.
- [ ] Root README CLI section replaced with real documentation.
- [ ] Command surface documented in `packages/cli/README.md`, matching this issue.
